metadata.title: HSBC upgrades Tesla, more than doubles target on SpaceX merger potential

content.text:
Investing.com -- HSBC has upgraded Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) to Hold from Reduce and raised its price target to $359 from $157, telling clients in a note on Friday that a potential merger with SpaceX (NASDAQ: SPCX) has shifted the focus to what an acquirer might pay.
Analyst Michael Tyndall noted that Elon Musk said on SpaceX's Oct. 20 earnings call that committees are reviewing a possible combination, though he gave no timeline.
HSBC said the business logic for a merger is not immediately clear, as the two companies serve very different customers. Instead, it believes the main motivation is control.
"We see control as the key motivation for a merger, especially as CEO Musk has been clear in the past about his need for oversight," Tyndall wrote.
Musk owns about 39% of SpaceX, which gives him 70% of the votes through its dual-class structure, compared with about 20% of Tesla.
"If we assume a 33% premium (in line with premium on recent similar transactions) to the trailing 30-day average share price, this gives an implied acquisition fair value for Tesla of USD507 per share. In the combined entity this would dilute CEO Musk's stake to c60%," HSBC said.
The bank also said adding Tesla could benefit SpaceX if both companies need to raise capital, as Tesla's spending needs are lower.
HSBC now values Tesla equally on its discounted cash flow model and the potential acquisition value. The new target still implies 6% downside.
"Given that the M&A topic is likely to dominate discussion, we see limited further downside from current levels and hence upgrade Tesla to Hold (from Reduce)," Tyndall said.
HSBC kept its Hold rating and $150 price target on SpaceX.
